summary:
We developed a full-stack Space Mission Design Game that enables individuals or teams of four to design, manage, and simulate complete space missions. Featuring a live 3D spacecraft builder, real-time resource dashboards, a global leaderboard, and an interactive arcade-style flight phase, our solution transforms abstract aerospace concepts into an engaging, hands-on experience.

Our project directly addresses the challenge by forcing players to navigate integrated engineering trade-offs. Powered by a custom physics evaluation engine, participants must balance strict constraints—including budget, mass, power generation, and data rates—across various instruments, power systems, and orbital configurations. Players instantly see the consequences of their decisions; for example, upgrading a scientific payload increases potential discoveries but immediately drains power and adds critical spacecraft mass.

This project is important because it bridges the gap between theoretical classroom learning and practical systems engineering. By providing immediate, visual feedback on how individual choices shape overall mission success, our game empowers the next generation of engineers to collaboratively solve complex problems and master the delicate balance required for real-world space exploration.
details:
Our Mission

Our Space Mission Design Game is an educational simulator where players design a spacecraft, balance critical resources (power, mass, budget, communications, and time), and pilot their creation in an arcade-style flight mission. As players select components, a 3D model of the spacecraft builds dynamically alongside a live resource dashboard. The game supports both solo play and team mode (with up to 4 roles). Once a mission concludes, players receive a post-mission analysis detailing why their design succeeded or failed, earn XP, unlock badges, and compete on a global leaderboard. To ensure fairness, a backend anti-cheat system recalculates the maximum possible score for each design code and automatically rejects mathematically impossible submissions.

Benefits and intended impact

The project was built to solve a core educational problem: the complex trade-offs of mission design are incredibly difficult to learn from textbooks alone. The primary benefit of our game is that it provides a hands-on environment where abstract constraints become immediate and visible. The intended impact is to empower students and space enthusiasts to intuitively understand aerospace engineering, enabling them to see a real-time 3D model of their work, make integrated decisions, and clearly grasp the specific engineering trade-offs required for a mission to succeed.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, or software used

We developed a decoupled, full-stack web application using the following technologies:

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript for the UI; Three.js for the interactive 3D spacecraft builder; and the HTML Canvas API for the arcade flight and mini-games.
  • Backend API: Python with FastAPI and SQLite to manage the REST API, player database, XP progression, and global leaderboard.
  • Physics Evaluator: A zero-dependency Java 17+ microservice that serves as an authoritative physics engine and anti-cheat validator.
  • Deployment & Testing: Docker and Docker Compose for streamlined containerization, and pytest for backend testing.
    README.md

How the project is creative

Our project creatively bridges the gap between rigorous systems engineering and highly engaging gameplay. Instead of relying purely on spreadsheets or static menus, we integrated a live 3D visualizer, interactive mini-games, and an arcade flight phase to make the consequences of engineering decisions visceral. Furthermore, our architectural approach is highly creative: we decoupled the game logic into a frontend UI while building a standalone Java evaluator service strictly to calculate the mathematical limits of a design, ensuring a tamper-proof global leaderboard.

Factors the team considered

  • Educational Accessibility: We deliberately simplified the physics model for educational purposes to ensure the concepts remain approachable for students.
  • Fairness and Security: We prioritized competitive integrity by implementing a robust anti-cheat system that rejects invalid scores and validates player names to prevent injection attacks.
  • Diverse Play Styles: We considered different skill levels by adding a non-ranked Sandbox mode for constraint-free experimentation, alongside a Team mode to foster collaboration.
  • Future Scalability: We acknowledged current limitations (such as the lack of authenticated user accounts) and laid the architectural groundwork for future expansions, including network-based cooperative multiplayer and expanded mission scenarios
